programme: RFX5 carries the RFX–CIITA arm of MHC class II transactivation almost by itself: its target list is essentially the class II locus (CIITA plus HLA-DMA, HLA-DMB, HLA-DOA, HLA-DOB, HLA-DPA1, HLA-DPB1, HLA-DQB2, HLA-DRA) together with HLA-E and HLA-F. CTCF, an architectural/insulator factor, shares HLA-E as a target; in general chromatin biology CTCF loops and compartmentalizes the extended MHC-II region so the RFX5–CIITA complex can act on it, giving the two factors a plausible physical relationship beyond co-occurrence in this list. TCF3 (E2A) supplies the B-lymphocyte side of the same cell-type context, driving CD79A, CD79B, PAX5, VPREB1, IGLL1 and PTCRA — the genes that assemble a B-cell receptor in the same lineage that expresses MHC-II to present antigen. Read together, RFX5, CTCF and TCF3 describe a lymphocyte antigen-presentation / B-cell programme rather than three independent regulators.
role_in_a: In blood, this programme would track how strongly circulating B cells and other MHC-II-bearing antigen-presenting cells are represented and activated — RFX5/CIITA setting HLA-D expression, TCF3 running the B-cell differentiation genes that accompany it. Any shift in fibromyalgia toward altered lymphocyte antigen presentation or B-cell activation in blood, a state proposed but not established for the disease, would move this module.
role_in_b: In colorectal tissue, the same module maps onto mucosal and gut-associated lymphoid activity: MHC-II-driven antigen presentation and B-cell/plasma-cell gene programming in the mucosa are the kind of change reported in subsets of IBS (notably post-infectious IBS) as part of low-grade mucosal immune activation, though again not a defining feature of the disease.
shared_axis: If both disorders involve a modest, tissue-appropriate rise in lymphocyte antigen-presentation activity — B cells and APCs in blood for fibromyalgia, mucosal lymphoid tissue for IBS — the same RFX5/CTCF/TCF3 module would be expected to recur in both, without either disease sharing a specific, named biological process beyond that generic immune-activation axis.
reasoning: The RFX5-centred MHC-II module is real and nameable from the target lists alone, and CTCF's shared HLA-E target gives it a plausible architectural role, but nothing in the retrieved record documents fibromyalgia and IBS sharing this axis, and the pairing is not obvious from anatomy (blood vs. colorectal mucosa) beyond a generic 'both involve some immune cells' argument. Open Targets shows no association for any factor in fibromyalgia and only a bottom-decile percentile for CTCF in IBS, so the account rests on general immunology reasoning rather than anything retrieved for this pair.
support: PMID 38662876 — describes CTCF-Related Disorder, a genetic haploinsufficiency syndrome whose phenotype includes irritable-bowel-type gastrointestinal symptoms; this is a Mendelian syndrome report, not a study of CTCF's role in idiopathic IBS, so it bears only tangentially on the module. No papers were retrieved for RFX5 or TCF3 in either disease.
how_to_falsify: In matched patient and control samples, quantify MHC class II surface expression (HLA-DR/DP/DQ) and CD79A/CD79B/PAX5 transcript levels on circulating B cells/monocytes from fibromyalgia patients and on mucosal lymphocytes/APCs from IBS biopsies; if RFX5/CIITA-driven MHC-II expression and TCF3-driven B-lineage genes are not coordinately elevated (or coordinately altered) relative to controls in either tissue, the shared lymphocyte antigen-presentation programme proposed here does not hold.
caveats: Only 16 patient-group comparisons and a single independent cohort pair back this result, so there is no cross-cohort replication. The tissues compared are not matched (blood for fibromyalgia, colorectal mucosa for IBS), so any 'shared immune programme' is inferred across compartments rather than observed in the same tissue. Critically, several of the most canonical lymphoid/antigen-presentation drivers — EBF1 (TCF3's usual B-cell partner), SPI1/PU.1, STAT3 and RELB — were removed as tissue-generic, meaning the regulators that would most directly signal a genuine, pair-specific lymphocyte-activation story were filtered out as generic blood/immune background; RFX5, CTCF and TCF3 sit at the edge of what distinguishes this pair from that background rather than clearly above it. PBX1 topped one patient group only and does not belong to the account.
